justification: Response-blind count of white-like flowers from the frozen phenotype stage. A pure function of the immutable input table, so any change at all is a defect rather than Monte Carlo noise.
Response-blind count of pigmented flowers from the frozen phenotype stage. Same reasoning as the white-like count.

Cross-fitted held-out AUC summarised over 1000 posterior draws of an INLA-SPDE fit that is not bit-deterministic across runs. 0.01 is roughly an order of magnitude above the draw-count Monte Carlo error and far below any margin that would change the model-diagnostic reading. The invariant keeps the reported discrimination clearly above chance-adjacent values.

Cross-fitted held-out RMSE on the standardised intensity scale, from the same non-deterministic posterior sampling. A 2 percent relative band absorbs draw noise while still catching a changed response, predictor set, or fold structure.

Mean fold AUC difference between two separately sampled INLA fits, so it carries the Monte Carlo error of both. The invariant is the published claim itself: the locked claim audit requires the national Bombus gain to stay below 0.02 in absolute value.

25-km partial regression slope computed from stage-02 cross-fitted residuals, which inherit posterior-sampling noise. The sign is what the claim rests on, together with the corrected p-value checked on its own row.

Restricted-permutation p-value on a 1000-permutation reference set (the reference value is exactly 28/1001). Its Monte Carlo standard error at p = 0.028 is sqrt(p(1-p)/1000) = 0.0052, so the tolerance is about 2.7 standard errors. The invariant is the significance threshold the manuscript relies on.
Companion 25-km partial slope for the pigmented-only intensity stage. Same reasoning as the presence slope.
Same 1000-permutation reference set and the same Monte Carlo argument as the presence stage; both belong to the same two-test correction family.
Count of 10-km environment-similar all-white-neighbour isolates. The isolate definition is response-blind and threshold-based, so the count is a deterministic function of the inputs.

Natural-null p-value from the same 1000-permutation grid (273/1001). Its Monte Carlo standard error at p = 0.27 is 0.014, and the tolerance is about three standard errors. The invariant is the tier statement itself: the isolate count must remain compatible with the natural model rather than becoming a positive finding.
Isolate count divided by the deterministic candidate denominator, hence deterministic for the same reason as the count.
Focal-minus-white-neighbour 5-km population rank difference. Exploratory human-context tier; only the sign is carried into the manuscript.

Benjamini-Hochberg corrected value over five population scales, from a raw p of 22/1001. The raw Monte Carlo standard error is 0.0046 and the correction inflates the value by a factor of about 3.5, giving roughly 0.016 on the corrected scale; the tolerance is about two of those. The invariant preserves the tier ceiling: this result must stay suggestive rather than crossing into significance.
Population-DID alignment contrast, exploratory sensitivity tier. As above, only the sign is carried.
Fraction of isolates in the DID-proximate high-population class (9 of 16). Numerator and denominator both come from response-blind threshold classifications of fixed rasters.
Count of cells meeting both the q10 unexpected-pigmentation and the top-10 DID-proximity-spike criteria. A deterministic intersection of two threshold sets.
